skill.name: denario
skill.description: Denario guides multiagent scientific research workflows from dataset context to methodology, results, and LaTeX paper generation.
skill.summary: Automates structured scientific research workflows with Denario agents.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static detections were false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline references, placeholders, or safe research examples. Confirmed risks include a curl-to-shell installer, privileged package installation, persistent shell profile credential setup, and Docker examples that expose API keys or service account files. No prompt injection attempts were found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell setup with a link to official Google Cloud SDK installation steps and checksum verification.

remediation.issue: Docker examples pass API keys and service account files into an unpinned image.
remediation.suggestion: Pin Docker images by digest and document least-privilege, short-lived credentials for container use.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance prints OPENAI_API_KEY with echo.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to check whether the variable is set without printing the secret value.

remediation.issue: Credential exports are suggested for shell startup files.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer session-scoped environment variables or a managed secret store instead of persistent shell profile entries.

remediation.issue: LaTeX installation uses sudo without warning.
remediation.suggestion: Add a confirmation note and offer Docker or user-scoped package options before privileged installation.

content.value_statement: Scientific workflows can stall when ideas, methods, analysis, and paper drafting are split across tools. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Denario workflows for data-driven research automation.
actual_capabilities: Defines Denario project setup and installation options for Python and Docker workflows.
Guides data description, idea generation, methodology creation, result generation, and paper generation stages.
Explains OpenAI and Google Vertex AI credential setup for Denario LLM backends.
Provides examples for climate analysis, medical imaging, machine learning, and time-series research.
Documents journal-oriented LaTeX paper generation, including APS formatting examples.
limitations: Requires external LLM provider credentials and may create cloud usage costs.
Generated research methods and conclusions still need expert validation before publication.
Computational results depend on installed dependencies, data quality, and local execution permissions.
LaTeX output may require a local TeX distribution or a containerized environment.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Research Project
use_cases.description: Turn dataset notes into a structured Denario workflow with research context, goals, and first analysis steps.

use_cases.title: Draft Methods and Results
use_cases.description: Use Denario stages to develop methodology, execute analysis, and organize findings for review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Manuscript
use_cases.description: Convert existing ideas, methods, and results into a journal-formatted LaTeX paper draft.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Research Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a dataset and research goal.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Denario to plan a research workflow for this dataset: [describe data]. Identify the data description, research goal, and first Denario steps.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Research Ideas
prompt_templates.scenario: Create candidate hypotheses from data context.
prompt_templates.prompt: Given this dataset context and available tools, help me use Denario to generate and compare three research ideas: [context].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Hybrid Method
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine a user-provided idea with automated methodology.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have this research idea: [idea]. Use Denario guidance to create a method plan, validation checks, and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced end-to-end workflow with publication output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible Denario pipeline for [domain]. Include data description, idea, method, execution review, figures, and LaTeX paper generation.

output_examples.input: Dataset with monthly temperature anomalies, statistical tools, and a goal to quantify warming trends.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow that defines climate data context, proposes a trend hypothesis, plans statistical tests, and prepares paper outputs.

output_examples.input: Completed traffic analysis results with model metrics, figures, and validation notes.
output_examples.output: A manuscript preparation plan with sections for methods, results, discussion, figures, and target journal formatting.

output_examples.input: Medical imaging dataset with labels, available deep learning tools, and an interpretability goal.
output_examples.output: A hybrid workflow that keeps the user research idea, asks Denario to draft methods, and adds review checkpoints before execution.

best_practices: Provide dataset size, format, known quality issues, domain context, and available analysis tools.
Review each generated idea, method, and result before moving to the next Denario stage.
Use least-privilege credentials and avoid printing or committing API keys.
anti_patterns: Running generated analysis without checking assumptions, data leakage, or validation design.
Treating generated paper text as publication-ready without expert review and citation checks.
Passing broad cloud credentials into unpinned containers or shared environments.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps guide Denario workflows for research ideas, methods, results, and LaTeX paper drafts.

faq.question: Does Denario run analysis code?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented get_results stage can execute computational analyses based on the generated methodology.

faq.question: Which LLM providers are described?
faq.answer: The documentation covers OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Anthropic-compatible interfaces, Azure OpenAI, and custom model endpoints.

faq.question: Can I use my own research idea?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow supports custom ideas, custom methods, and precomputed results.

faq.question: Does it create journal-formatted papers?
faq.answer: Yes. The references describe LaTeX generation and an APS journal formatting example.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing?
faq.answer: Review data assumptions, statistical validity, generated claims, citations, figures, and all credential handling steps.
